papers.title: ReTAC: Residual Test-Time Agentic Computation for Video Spatial Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Test-time agentic computation can improve multimodal large language models (MLLMs) through planning, tool use, iterative perception, and reflection, but indiscriminate computation may duplicate resolved work, introduce noisy evidence, and perturb correct predictions. We propose that such computation should be residual: allocate additional computation only to requirements unresolved by the base model and, after a localized failure, recompute only the affected states. We instantiate this formulation in ReTAC, a training-free multiagent framework for video spatial reasoning. ReTAC organizes supplementary computation around unresolved requirements. It plans ordered steps to acquire missing spatial evidence and combines the observations with compatible native evidence for reasoning. In addition, it uses stage-aligned verification to localize failures to planning, perception, or reasoning. Dependency-based recovery recomputes only affected states while reusing unaffected ones. Extensive experiments show that ReTAC achieves the highest overall score among the compared methods across three mainstream MLLMs and two widely adopted benchmarks. Further analyses show that gains from additional computation depend not only on how much is used, but also on where it is allocated and which valid intermediate states are preserved.
papers.abstract_zh: 测试时智能体计算可以通过规划、工具使用、迭代感知和反思来改进多模态大语言模型（MLLMs），但不加区分的计算可能会重复已完成的工作、引入噪声证据并扰动正确的预测。我们提出此类计算应当是残差的：仅将额外计算分配给基础模型未解决的需求，并且在局部失败后仅重新计算受影响的状态。我们在 ReTAC 中实例化了这一构想，这是一个用于视频空间推理的免训练多智能体框架。ReTAC 围绕未解决的需求组织补充计算。它规划有序步骤以获取缺失的空间证据，并将观察结果与兼容的固有证据结合用于推理。此外，它使用阶段对齐的验证将失败定位到规划、感知或推理。基于依赖关系的恢复仅重新计算受影响的状态，同时复用未受影响的状态。大量实验表明，在三个主流 MLLM 和两个广泛采用的基准上，ReTAC 在对比方法中取得了最高的总体得分。进一步分析表明，额外计算带来的收益不仅取决于使用了多少计算，还取决于计算被分配到哪里以及哪些有效的中间状态被保留。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出免训练多智能体框架 ReTAC，将测试时计算残差化，仅针对基础模型未解决的需求分配计算并只重算受影响状态，在视频空间推理的三个 MLLM 与两个基准上取得最高总体得分。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DriveWLA: Unifying Future Dynamics and Scene Semantics through World-Language-Action Modeling for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and world models have demonstrated strong capabilities in semantic understanding and future scene evolution for autonomous driving. However, effectively integrating both capabilities for trajectory generation remains challenging. In this work, we propose DriveWLA, a unified World-Language-Action model based on Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) that jointly models semantic understanding, future scene dynamics, and trajectory generation. DriveWLA consists of three experts: a World Expert for future prediction, a Language Expert for semantic understanding, and an Action Expert for trajectory generation. We further introduce Cross-Expert Attention, which enables controlled information flow across experts while aligning semantic and dynamic representations. To improve trajectory generation beyond imitation learning, we apply Flow-GRPO reinforcement learning post-training to refine the Action Expert. Extensive experiments show that DriveWLA achieves superior performance in both open-loop and closed-loop evaluation. DriveWLA achieves 92.3 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, demonstrating strong performance among VLM-based and world-model-based planners. Without specific fine-tuning, DriveWLA further demonstrates strong zero-shot generalization to HUGSIM, nuScenes, and Bench2Drive. These results validate the effectiveness of our unified World-Language-Action modeling, establishing DriveWLA as a generalizable framework for autonomous driving.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）和世界模型在自动驾驶的语义理解和未来场景演化方面已展现出强大能力。然而，有效整合这两种能力以生成轨迹仍然具有挑战性。在这项工作中，我们提出 DriveWLA，一个基于 Transformer 混合（MoT）的统一世界-语言-动作模型，联合建模语义理解、未来场景动态和轨迹生成。DriveWLA 由三个专家组成：用于未来预测的世界专家、用于语义理解的语言专家和用于轨迹生成的动作专家。我们进一步引入跨专家注意力，它在对齐语义和动态表示的同时实现跨专家的受控信息流。为了超越模仿学习改进轨迹生成，我们应用 Flow-GRPO 强化学习后训练来精炼动作专家。大量实验表明，DriveWLA 在开环和闭环评估中均取得优越性能。DriveWLA 在 NAVSIM v1 上达到 92.3 PDMS，在 NAVSIM v2 上达到 90.1 EPDMS，在基于 VLM 和基于世界模型的规划器中展现出强劲性能。无需特定微调，DriveWLA 进一步展现出对 HUGSIM、nuScenes 和 Bench2Drive 的强大零样本泛化能力。这些结果验证了我们统一世界-语言-动作建模的有效性，确立了 DriveWLA 作为自动驾驶可泛化框架的地位。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 Transformer 混合的统一世界-语言-动作模型 DriveWLA，通过世界、语言、动作三个专家与跨专家注意力联合建模，并用 Flow-GRPO 后训练精炼动作专家，在 NAVSIM v1/v2 上分别达到 92.3 PDMS 和 90.1 EPDMS，并零样本泛化到 HUGSIM、nuScenes 和 Bench2Drive。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training

papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.abstract_en: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
papers.abstract_zh: 长上下文大语言模型中注意力机制的设计面临 KV 缓存大小、训练与预填充 FLOPs 以及模型质量之间的“不可能三角”。GQA 取得了良好的质量，但带来较高的 KV 缓存开销；MLA 和 MFA 等替代方法可以压缩缓存，但 MLA 存在质量损失，而 MFA 大幅增加训练和预填充计算量。我们提出虚拟头注意力（VHA），它通过两个轻量线性操作同时改善这三个顶点：Q Premix 对每个 KV 组内的查询施加近似恒等变换，从减半的物理查询头中恢复虚拟头多样性；Linear Postmix 通过低秩的 $I + AB^\top$ 残差结构融合头间特征。由于 VHA 不引入非线性操作，推理时 Premix 可以折叠进查询投影，Postmix 可以折叠进输出投影，使模型退化为标准 GQA-2 架构，从而直接复用所有现有的 GQA 推理优化。仅使用两个 KV 头时，大模型中的组大小很容易达到 64，在解码期间充分利用 Tensor Core 并行性。在 4K 上下文、500 亿 token 预训练的四个规模上，VHA 在每个规模上都持续超越标准 GQA 基线（+0.05% 至 +0.81%），同时在稠密规模上将 KV 缓存相比 GQA-8 减少 4 倍、在 MoE 规模上相比 GQA-4 减少 2 倍，并将训练和预填充 FLOPs 降低 7.9%（1.7B，$S{=}4096$）。在一个以 8K 上下文、5000 亿 token 训练的工业级 30B-A3B MoE 模型上，VHA 在 12 项基准的基础模型评估套件上分别超越 MLA 和 GQA-4 达 +0.70% 和 +2.60%；在另一项匹配的 10B-A1B MoE 长上下文中期训练对比中，VHA 在 8K–128K 上取得平均 RULER 分数 84.4，而 GQA 为 73.0，同时在全注意力层中使用两个而非四个 KV 头。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出虚拟头注意力 VHA，通过 Q Premix 与低秩 Linear Postmix 两个可折叠线性操作，在减少 KV 缓存与训练/预填充 FLOPs 的同时提升质量，四个规模预训练均超越 GQA 基线，并在 30B-A3B MoE 上优于 MLA 和 GQA-4。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
匹配 模型架构：attention mechanism

papers.title: FRACTION: Fraud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context Navigation
papers.abstract_en: Graph fraud explanation generation emerges as an important task, which requires jointly leveraging graph structure and content information to produce human-readable explanations for a given risk label. An intuitive approach is to adapt existing graph-enhanced large language models (LLMs), which inject graph structure into LLMs via graph-conditioned instruction tuning or structure-aware embeddings. However, existing methods face two key challenges in graph fraud explanation generation: a lack of evaluation protocols tailored to explanation quality, and a mismatch between the granularity of graph information they provide and what explanation generation requires. In this paper, we propose FRaud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context NavigaTION (FRACTION), a framework for graph fraud explanation generation. To evaluate explanation quality, we introduce a task-specific rubric that assesses faithfulness, graph grounding, helpfulness, consistency, and conciseness, and validate it against human judgments. To focus on fine-grained details of relevant neighbors without reading the entire neighborhood, we equip a language model with graph tools that progressively disclose neighbor records. To train our graph agent, we propose a rubric-guided trajectory distillation strategy through which the agent learns both tool-use behavior and structured explanation generation. Experimental results on three fraud datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines under a human-aligned rubric.
papers.abstract_zh: 图欺诈解释生成作为一项重要任务出现，它需要联合利用图结构和内容信息，为给定的风险标签生成人类可读的解释。一种直观的方法是改造现有的图增强大语言模型（LLMs），它们通过图条件指令微调或结构感知嵌入将图结构注入 LLM。然而，现有方法在图欺诈解释生成中面临两个关键挑战：缺乏针对解释质量定制的评估协议，以及它们提供的图信息粒度与解释生成所需粒度之间的不匹配。在本文中，我们提出 FRaud Explanation Generation via Agentic Graph Context NavigaTION（FRACTION），一个用于图欺诈解释生成的框架。为了评估解释质量，我们引入一个任务特定的评分标准，评估忠实性、图依据性、有用性、一致性和简洁性，并对照人类判断进行验证。为了在不读取整个邻域的情况下聚焦相关邻居的细粒度细节，我们为语言模型配备图工具，逐步披露邻居记录。为了训练我们的图智能体，我们提出一种评分标准引导的轨迹蒸馏策略，智能体通过该策略学习工具使用行为和结构化解释生成。在三个欺诈数据集上的实验结果表明，在与人类对齐的评分标准下，相比最先进的基线取得了一致改进。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出图欺诈解释生成框架 FRACTION，引入评估忠实性、图依据性、有用性、一致性和简洁性的任务评分标准，为语言模型配备逐步披露邻居记录的图工具，并用评分标准引导的轨迹蒸馏训练图智能体，在三个欺诈数据集上一致优于最先进基线。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Genesis: Visual Augmentation Primitives for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Recent multimodal large language models achieve promising results on visual reasoning tasks, approaching human-level performance on existing STEM benchmarks. However, these capabilities degrade under complex real-world scenes. We identify that chain-of-thought reasoning remains largely confined to the linguistic space, rarely anchoring each step in visual evidence. The main cause is the absence of such data during training. In this work, we introduce a training data augmentation pipeline, \textbf{Visual Augmentation Primitives} (VAP), which leverages state-of-the-art vision generative models to synthesize diverse photorealistic training samples and corresponding reasoning text. VAP introduces some basic operators and applies them to a seed image and gets a variant. It also constructs coherent multimodal reasoning chains throughout the generation process. Such training data force models to perceive visual content and perform logical reasoning according to them at every step. We further introduce multimodal chain-of-thought rubric-based reinforcement learning to enhance this. It rewards not only text reasoning but also visual reasoning by scoring intermediate reasoning steps for logical validity, completeness, and consistency. Moreover, we construct the UNREAL benchmark to systematically evaluate visual reasoning on hyperrealistic scenes across controllable difficulty levels. Experiments show that a 4B model built on this framework surpasses 8B baselines, with performance improving consistently as the model scales to 32B, validating the scaling law for visual reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期多模态大语言模型在视觉推理任务上取得了有前景的结果，在现有 STEM 基准上接近人类水平表现。然而，这些能力在复杂真实场景下会退化。我们发现思维链推理在很大程度上仍局限于语言空间，很少将每一步锚定在视觉证据上。主要原因是训练期间缺乏此类数据。在这项工作中，我们引入一个训练数据增强流水线，\textbf{Visual Augmentation Primitives}（VAP），它利用最先进的视觉生成模型合成多样化的照片级真实训练样本及相应的推理文本。VAP 引入一些基本算子并将其应用于种子图像以得到一个变体。它还在整个生成过程中构建连贯的多模态推理链。此类训练数据迫使模型在每一步感知视觉内容并据此进行逻辑推理。我们进一步引入基于评分标准的多模态思维链强化学习来增强这一点。它不仅奖励文本推理，还通过对中间推理步骤的逻辑有效性、完整性和一致性进行评分来奖励视觉推理。此外，我们构建 UNREAL 基准，以在可控难度级别上系统评估超写实场景中的视觉推理。实验表明，基于该框架构建的 4B 模型超越了 8B 基线，并且随着模型扩展到 32B 性能持续提升，验证了视觉推理的缩放定律。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出视觉增强原语（VAP）训练数据增强流水线，用视觉生成模型合成照片级样本与连贯多模态推理链，并结合基于评分标准的多模态思维链强化学习，使 4B 模型超越 8B 基线且性能随规模扩展至 32B 持续提升。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) improve parameter efficiency by recursively reusing shared Transformer modules, yet their repeated computation over evolving recurrent states poses new challenges for low-bit deployment. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods, largely designed for feed-forward Transformers, fail to account for cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation, leading to substantial performance degradation at low precision. To address these challenges, we propose LoopQuant, a loop-aware PTQ framework for accurate and efficient low-bit quantization of LoopLMs. LoopQuant is built on three core components: 1) Cross-Loop Distribution Canonicalization (CLDC) learns a shared quantization-friendly representation across recurrent states while preserving parameter sharing; 2) Interaction-Aware Loop-wise Precision Allocation (ILPA) allocates activation precision under a fixed bit budget by modeling task-level loop sensitivity and cross-loop interactions; and 3) Loop-Conditioned Task Calibration (LCTC) further aligns quantized inference with the low-bit recursive trajectory through lightweight task-space calibration. Extensive experiments across LoopLM architectures demonstrate that LoopQuant consistently outperforms existing low-bit PTQ methods. On Ouro-2.6B, LoopQuant under W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines in performance, while reducing model memory by 65.3% with only 3.4% additional storage overhead over naive INT4 and achieving a 1.7 times decoding speedup over BF16. These results demonstrate a strong balance among accuracy, compression, and inference efficiency, providing a practical and deployment-friendly solution for low-bit LoopLM inference. The code is available at [https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/LoopQuant].
papers.abstract_zh: 循环语言模型（LoopLMs）通过递归复用共享的 Transformer 模块来提升参数效率，但其在不断演化的循环状态上重复计算，为低比特部署带来了新的挑战。现有训练后量化（PTQ）方法大多面向前馈 Transformer 设计，未能考虑跨循环的激活动态、异构的循环敏感性和递归误差传播，导致低精度下性能大幅下降。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 LoopQuant，一个面向 LoopLM 的循环感知 PTQ 框架，可实现准确且高效的低比特量化。LoopQuant 建立在三个核心组件之上：1）跨循环分布规范化（CLDC）在保持参数共享的同时，学习跨循环状态的共享量化友好表示；2）交互感知的逐循环精度分配（ILPA）在固定比特预算下，通过建模任务级循环敏感性和跨循环交互来分配激活精度；3）循环条件任务校准（LCTC）通过轻量级任务空间校准，进一步使量化推理与低比特递归轨迹对齐。跨 LoopLM 架构的大量实验表明，LoopQuant 持续优于现有低比特 PTQ 方法。在 Ouro-2.6B 上，LoopQuant 在 W4A4 下的性能超过所有 W4A8 基线，同时相比朴素 INT4 将模型内存减少 65.3%，仅增加 3.4% 的额外存储开销，并相比 BF16 实现 1.7 倍的解码加速。这些结果展示了在准确率、压缩和推理效率之间的良好平衡，为低比特 LoopLM 推理提供了实用且易于部署的解决方案。代码见 [https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/LoopQuant]。
papers.tldr_zh: LoopQuant 提出循环感知的训练后量化框架，通过跨循环分布规范化、逐循环精度分配和循环条件任务校准，在 Ouro-2.6B 上以 W4A4 超过 W4A8 基线，内存减少 65.3% 并实现 1.7 倍解码加速。

papers.title: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在视频问答上取得了强劲结果，但往往无法恢复使视频连贯的时间结构。它们可能合并相邻事件、遗漏单一事件的进展，或推断出跨事件的不合理关系。我们将结构化时间理解研究为从视觉证据中恢复事件结构的能力，包括事件边界、单一事件进展和多事件关系。我们认为这一差距源于当前后训练目标与时间推理之间的不匹配，其中字幕式监督使模型依赖语言捷径而非视觉时间基础。为此，我们提出 EventLens，一个以视觉为中心的强化学习框架，通过事件结构恢复来学习视频理解。EventLens 不重建字幕，而是训练模型在受控扰动下恢复时间结构，例如改变时间粒度、反转进展和打乱事件顺序。我们用一个三级时间本体实例化该框架，并推导出三个可验证的任务族：事件分割、进展判别和多事件关系推理。这些任务具有确定性奖励，使得无需人类偏好标签或学习奖励模型即可进行任务专用的 GRPO 训练。我们进一步引入多教师在线策略蒸馏（MT-OPD），将专用策略整合为统一模型。在 Qwen3-VL 骨干上的实验表明，在时间基础和事件敏感推理基准上取得一致提升，同时保持通用视频问答性能。学习曲线进一步表明，与直接混合 RL 优化相比，EventLens 以显著降低的训练成本实现了可比的下游迁移。
papers.tldr_zh: EventLens 提出以视觉为中心的强化学习框架，通过事件分割、进展判别和多事件关系推理三类可验证任务及多教师在线策略蒸馏，在 Qwen3-VL 上提升时间基础与事件敏感推理，同时保持通用视频问答性能。

papers.title: LLM Agents for Automated Post-Training via Structured Recipe Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Automated post-training transforms pre-trained large language models (LLMs) into models capable of handling diverse domains by automatically constructing and optimizing a recipe of coupled decisions over data sources, data processing, cross-domain composition, and training configuration under a limited experimental budget. Existing automation either searches predefined recipe spaces that enable systematic optimization but remain fixed rather than adapting their available choices to the target tasks, or uses open-ended agents that discover task-specific choices but leave them implicit in trial-level edits, limiting their systematic reuse and recombination across trials. To fill this gap, we introduce optimization over a task-adapted recipe space, a novel paradigm that can adapt the recipe space itself to the target tasks while representing its choices explicitly for systematic reuse, recombination, and joint optimization. We instantiate this paradigm with Structured Recipe Optimization (SRO), comprising an LLM-based Recipe-Space Designer that constructs the task-adapted recipe space and a Multi-Domain Recipe Optimizer that uses structured trial evidence to guide LLM candidate construction and multi-objective Bayesian trial selection. Extensive experiments show that SRO achieves the highest average score in all evaluated target-model and agent-LLM combinations. In joint post-training across three capability domains and six benchmarks, SRO reaches 41.1 versus 15.4 for the strongest baseline on Qwen3-1.7B with GPT-5.4, and 53.8 versus 40.8 on Qwen3-4B with DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Our code is available at https://github.com/RuohLiuq/SRO.
papers.abstract_zh: 自动化后训练通过在有限实验预算下自动构建和优化数据源、数据处理、跨域组合和训练配置等耦合决策的方案，将预训练大语言模型（LLMs）转化为能够处理多样领域的模型。现有自动化方法要么搜索预定义的方案空间，虽能系统优化但空间固定，无法根据目标任务调整可用选择；要么使用开放式智能体发现任务特定选择，但这些选择隐含在试验级编辑中，限制了跨试验的系统性复用和重组。为填补这一空白，我们引入任务自适应方案空间上的优化，这一新范式能够使方案空间本身适应目标任务，同时显式表示其选择以支持系统性复用、重组和联合优化。我们以结构化方案优化（SRO）实例化该范式，包含一个基于 LLM 的方案空间设计器来构建任务自适应方案空间，以及一个多域方案优化器，利用结构化试验证据指导 LLM 候选构建和多目标贝叶斯试验选择。大量实验表明，SRO 在所有评估的目标模型与智能体 LLM 组合中取得最高平均分。在跨三个能力域和六个基准的联合后训练中，SRO 在 Qwen3-1.7B 搭配 GPT-5.4 上达到 41.1，而最强基线为 15.4；在 Qwen3-4B 搭配 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 上达到 53.8，而基线为 40.8。代码见 https://github.com/RuohLiuq/SRO。
papers.tldr_zh: SRO 提出任务自适应方案空间上的优化范式，用 LLM 方案空间设计器与多域方案优化器实现自动化后训练，在 Qwen3-1.7B/GPT-5.4 和 Qwen3-4B/DeepSeek-V4-Flash 上分别取得 41.1 对 15.4、53.8 对 40.8 的平均分。

papers.title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions
papers.abstract_en: Foundation models for tables and relational databases are increasingly used for predictive tasks across various scientific and industrial domains. However, adapting existing models to unseen datasets requires tens of thousands of examples. Here we introduce RT-J, an 85M-parameter relational foundation model (RFM) that makes accurate predictions even with hundreds of in-context examples or fewer. To achieve this, we first assemble the Join, a large collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks. We pretrain with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells, using in-context examples from a novel lightweight random-walk retriever. Finally, we leverage context tuning and ensembling to scale up test-time compute. On in-context regression tasks from RelBench, RT-J requires 10x fewer examples on average to match strong feature engineering pipelines with LLM-agent or RDBLearn featurizers and TabICLv2 or LightGBM predictors. Overall, our work pushes the frontier for context-efficient predictions on relational data and highlights the importance of real-world semantics, context engineering and large-scale pretraining for RFMs.
papers.abstract_zh: 面向表格和关系数据库的基础模型正越来越多地用于各科学和工业领域的预测任务。然而，将现有模型适配到未见数据集需要数万个样本。在此我们提出 RT-J，一个 85M 参数的关系基础模型（RFM），即使仅有数百个或更少的上下文示例也能做出准确预测。为此，我们首先构建 Join，一个包含 639 个网络爬取数据库和 6,023 个 LLM 生成预测任务的大型集合。我们使用长达 8,192 个数据库单元的长上下文进行预训练，上下文示例来自一种新颖的轻量级随机游走检索器。最后，我们利用上下文调优和集成来扩展测试时计算。在 RelBench 的上下文回归任务上，RT-J 平均需要少 10 倍的示例即可匹配使用 LLM 智能体或 RDBLearn 特征化器以及 TabICLv2 或 LightGBM 预测器的强特征工程流水线。总体而言，我们的工作推进了关系数据上上下文高效预测的前沿，并凸显了真实世界语义、上下文工程和大规模预训练对 RFM 的重要性。
papers.tldr_zh: RT-J 是一个 85M 参数的关系基础模型，基于 639 个数据库和 6,023 个任务、最长 8,192 单元上下文预训练，在 RelBench 上下文回归上平均少用 10 倍示例即可匹配强特征工程流水线。

papers.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11\% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.
papers.abstract_zh: 投机解码（SD）已被证明能有效加速大语言模型推理，但对于视觉语言模型（VLMs），多样的输入模态使小型训练草稿模型难以持续实现高吞吐。自投机解码复用目标模型的部分作为草稿模型，保留了 VLM 的多模态能力，但其效率取决于为每个提示选择合适的草稿配置。我们提出单峰投机解码（SP$^2$ec），一种无需训练的 bandit 算法，在生成过程中自适应调整草稿配置。SP$^2$ec 利用了现有自投机方法（包括 SWIFT、KnapSpec、SpecVLM 以及我们简单的 cosSim）中观察到的单峰吞吐模式。我们的算法设计显式最小化针对每个给定查询的新颖墙钟时间遗憾概念，对应经验墙钟延迟。墙钟时间遗憾的理论保证表明，SP$^2$ec 能够利用最优草稿配置，且探索成本可忽略。在 Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 和 LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B 上跨视觉和文本任务的大量实验表明，相比原始自投机方法持续提升最高达 11\%，展示了所提 SP$^2$ec 算法的广泛适用性。
papers.tldr_zh: SP$^2$ec 是一种无需训练、基于 bandit 的自投机解码方法，利用单峰吞吐模式在生成中自适应调整草稿配置，在 Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct 和 LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B 上相比原始自投机方法最高提升 11%。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm

papers.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
papers.abstract_en: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines. Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex. Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents' robustness to noise while maintaining stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型已从单轮聊天机器人演变为能够进行长时程推理的交互式智能体。在实际部署中，MCP 工具服务可能返回带噪声的反馈，用户也可能介入纠正智能体，但现有方法对反思学习与失败恢复提供的监督有限。为弥补这一差距，我们提出 Agent-Reflex，一个用于激励智能体主动反思的通用训练框架。具体而言，Agent-Reflex 包含三个阶段。首先，环境反思技能发现（RSD）在环境扩展中注入有依据的工具反馈扰动，采样能力多样的 LLM 池，挖掘匹配的成功-失败对，并总结可复用的反思元技能。在此技能库基础上，我们应用反思监督微调（ReSFT），将每项技能转化为对自我反思、技能恢复和以用户为中心的纠正的监督，强化互补的反思行为。最后，我们提出同策略反思策略优化（ORPO），将噪声交互下的智能体强化学习与反思引导的同策略蒸馏相结合，以进一步激发主动反思。基于 Qwen3-8B，Agent-Reflex 在五个长时程工具使用基准上达到 58.6 的总体成绩，在 AgentNoiseBench 上达到 29.1，超越了强大的环境扩展与反思基线。在六个具有挑战性的智能体基准套件上的实验证明了 Agent-Reflex 的有效性。进一步分析表明，Agent-Reflex 提升了智能体对噪声的鲁棒性，同时保持稳定的训练动态，支持可扩展的智能体训练。我们的代码见 https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex。
papers.tldr_zh: Agent-Reflex 通过环境反思技能发现、反思监督微调和同策略反思策略优化三阶段训练框架，激励语言智能体主动反思，在长时程工具使用与噪声交互基准上超越环境扩展和反思基线。

papers.title: MicroCLIP: Connecting Text and Microscopy Images via Contrastive Language--Image Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Understanding fluorescence microscopy images is fundamental to automating biological research. However, existing methods typically learn predefined concepts from closed-set data, limiting transfer across tasks and biological contexts. In this work, we introduce MicroCLIP, a vision-language model that learns generalizable cellular and subcellular representations from natural language supervision for open-set image classification and retrieval. To pretrain MicroCLIP, we construct MicroPool-2M, a dataset of approximately 2.5 million fluorescence microscopy image-text pairs spanning diverse cellular structures, cell lines, and imaging conditions. Aligning microscopy images with biological concepts in natural language is challenging because most images lack descriptive captions and biological knowledge annotations. We therefore progressively establish image-text associations at three levels to provide MicroCLIP with richer semantic supervision: (1) category-level alignment links images to standardized labels defined by subcellular structure-cell-line combinations; (2) knowledge-level alignment incorporates biological priors derived from these labels to capture relationships across species and cell types; and (3) detail-level alignment uses a multimodal large language model to recaption and verify image-text pairs at scale, emphasizing fine-grained visual characteristics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MicroCLIP achieves leading performance in zero-shot classification and text-image retrieval on microscopy images. It retrieves images with specific cellular characteristics from thousands of candidates and generalizes to unseen biological concepts without additional supervision. These results highlight MicroCLIP's potential as a foundation model for fluorescence microscopy.
papers.abstract_zh: 理解荧光显微图像是自动化生物学研究的基础。然而，现有方法通常从闭集数据中学习预定义概念，限制了跨任务和跨生物语境的迁移。在本工作中，我们提出 MicroCLIP，一个视觉-语言模型，从自然语言监督中学习可泛化的细胞与亚细胞表征，用于开集图像分类和检索。为预训练 MicroCLIP，我们构建了 MicroPool-2M，一个约 250 万荧光显微图像-文本对的数据集，涵盖多样的细胞结构、细胞系和成像条件。将显微图像与自然语言中的生物学概念对齐具有挑战性，因为大多数图像缺乏描述性标题和生物学知识标注。因此，我们在三个层次上逐步建立图像-文本关联，为 MicroCLIP 提供更丰富的语义监督：（1）类别级对齐将图像链接到由亚细胞结构-细胞系组合定义的标准化标签；（2）知识级对齐引入由这些标签导出的生物学先验，以捕捉跨物种和细胞类型的关系；（3）细节级对齐使用多模态大语言模型大规模重写标题并验证图像-文本对，强调细粒度视觉特征。大量实验表明，MicroCLIP 在显微图像的零样本分类和文本-图像检索上取得领先性能。它能够从数千个候选中检索具有特定细胞特征的图像，并在无额外监督的情况下泛化到未见过的生物学概念。这些结果凸显了 MicroCLIP 作为荧光显微基础模型的潜力。
papers.tldr_zh: MicroCLIP 构建约 250 万图像-文本对的 MicroPool-2M 数据集，通过类别级、知识级和细节级三层对齐进行对比语言-图像预训练，在荧光显微图像的零样本分类与检索上取得领先性能。

papers.title: TwinPrune: Density-Aware Two-Phase Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: We propose a unified spatial-density signal to score token importance for both inference phases: bipartite merge for prefill and KV eviction for decode, yielding measurable gains in each stage. To isolate the two phases, we split benchmarks by scoring logic. Prefill probes (MMBench, POPE, ScienceQA) evaluate only the first decoded token; their accuracy reflects prefill logits argmax before any decode KV eviction. Full-pipeline probes (TextVQA, DocVQA, MM-Vet) assess the complete generated sequence and capture both phases. We identify a critical evaluation pitfall: decode pruning claims validated solely on prefill probes measure prefill quality, not decode performance. Experiments show discarding all visual KV during decode barely affects prefill-probe accuracy but degrades TextVQA and MM-Vet drastically; this insensitivity stems from the scoring rule, not compression intensity.Evaluated on seven model variants (InternVL-3.5, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA-1.5) and three full-pipeline benchmarks, our method achieves a three-way Pareto frontier across compute, memory and accuracy. Density-based prefill compression maintains strong accuracy, scales linearly with visual token count, and delivers 100x faster token selection at high resolution. For decode, density top-k KV eviction consistently outperforms strong baselines H2O, SnapKV and StreamingLLM on TextVQA and MM-Vet across three retention ratios. At 0.125 keep ratio on TextVQA, it surpasses H2O by 9.6 points; InternVL-3.5 models (2B to 38B) maintain a 7 to 10 point advantage. Compression scales favorably with model size: every measured 8B to 38B model transition reduces accuracy loss instead of worsening it. We suggest MM-Vet or DocVQA as mandatory full-pipeline validation for any decode-phase claims. Our code is available at https://github.com/Kai-Liu001/TwinPrune
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出一种统一的空间密度信号，用于为两个推理阶段评分 token 重要性：预填充阶段的双部合并与解码阶段的 KV 驱逐，从而在每个阶段都带来可测量的收益。为隔离这两个阶段，我们按评分逻辑划分基准。预填充探针（MMBench、POPE、ScienceQA）仅评估第一个解码 token；其准确率反映任何解码 KV 驱逐之前的预填充 logits argmax。全流程探针（TextVQA、DocVQA、MM-Vet）评估完整生成序列，捕捉两个阶段。我们发现一个关键评估陷阱：仅用预填充探针验证的解码剪枝主张实际测量的是预填充质量，而非解码性能。实验表明，在解码期间丢弃所有视觉 KV 几乎不影响预填充探针准确率，但会大幅降低 TextVQA 和 MM-Vet；这种不敏感性源于评分规则，而非压缩强度。在七个模型变体（InternVL-3.5、Qwen3-VL、LLaVA-1.5）和三个全流程基准上评估，我们的方法在计算、内存和准确率上实现三向帕累托前沿。基于密度的预填充压缩保持强劲准确率，随视觉 token 数量线性扩展，并在高分辨率下实现 100 倍更快的 token 选择。对于解码，基于密度的 top-k KV 驱逐在 TextVQA 和 MM-Vet 上于三种保留率下持续优于强基线 H2O、SnapKV 和 StreamingLLM。在 TextVQA 上 0.125 保留率时，它比 H2O 高出 9.6 分；InternVL-3.5 模型（2B 至 38B）保持 7 至 10 分的优势。压缩随模型规模有利扩展：每个实测的 8B 到 38B 模型过渡都减少而非加重准确率损失。我们建议将 MM-Vet 或 DocVQA 作为任何解码阶段主张的强制全流程验证。我们的代码见 https://github.com/Kai-Liu001/TwinPrune。
papers.tldr_zh: TwinPrune 提出统一空间密度信号，在预填充阶段进行双部合并、在解码阶段进行 KV 驱逐，并指出仅用预填充探针验证解码剪枝的评估陷阱，在七个模型变体和三个全流程基准上实现计算、内存与准确率的三向帕累托前沿。

papers.title: MultiAlloc: Budget-Aware Precision Allocation for KV Cache Quantization
papers.abstract_en: The Key-Value (KV) cache constitutes a dominant source of memory consumption during large language model (LLM) inference, particularly in long-context and complex reasoning scenarios. Existing KV cache quantization methods have explored different compression granularities, including layer-wise precision adjustment and token-level information preservation. In practical deployment, however, the key challenge is not merely compression, but how to allocate limited quantization resources among heterogeneous precision preservation strategies under a fixed KV cache memory budget. We propose MultiAlloc, a profiling-guided precision allocation framework for KV cache quantization that adaptively distributes limited quantization resources between layer-wise precision enhancement and token-wise preservation. MultiAlloc employs lightweight offline profiling to characterize layer sensitivity and token importance, enabling adaptive precision allocation under a fixed memory constraint. Guided by the profiled memory--accuracy trade-off, it automatically derives an effective precision allocation strategy without online allocation search, and applies the resulting policy during inference. Extensive experiments on reasoning and long-context benchmarks demonstrate that MultiAlloc consistently improves over layer-wise, token-wise, and recent multi-granularity KV cache quantization methods under matched memory budgets across diverse models, including Mistral, Llama, DeepSeek-Qwen, and QwQ.
papers.abstract_zh: 键值（KV）缓存是大语言模型（LLM）推理期间内存消耗的主要来源，在长上下文和复杂推理场景中尤为突出。现有 KV 缓存量化方法探索了不同的压缩粒度，包括逐层精度调整和 token 级信息保留。然而在实际部署中，关键挑战不仅是压缩，而是如何在固定 KV 缓存内存预算下，在异构的精度保留策略之间分配有限的量化资源。我们提出 MultiAlloc，一个面向 KV 缓存量化的剖析引导精度分配框架，自适应地在逐层精度增强与 token 级保留之间分配有限的量化资源。MultiAlloc 采用轻量级离线剖析来刻画层敏感性和 token 重要性，从而在固定内存约束下实现自适应精度分配。在剖析得到的内存-准确率权衡指导下，它无需在线分配搜索即可自动推导出有效的精度分配策略，并在推理期间应用所得策略。在推理和长上下文基准上的大量实验表明，在匹配内存预算下，MultiAlloc 在包括 Mistral、Llama、DeepSeek-Qwen 和 QwQ 在内的多种模型上持续优于逐层、token 级以及近期多粒度 KV 缓存量化方法。
papers.tldr_zh: MultiAlloc 通过轻量级离线剖析刻画层敏感性与 token 重要性，在固定 KV 缓存内存预算下自适应地在逐层精度增强与 token 级保留之间分配量化资源，在多种模型和基准上优于逐层、token 级及多粒度量化方法。

papers.title: Label-Centric Knowledge Retrieval for Zero-Shot Text Classification
papers.abstract_en: Flagship large language models (LLMs) offer rich general knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, but their high inference cost and latency limit their use for large-scale data labeling. We study zero-shot text classification with semantically meaningful labels and task descriptions, without task-specific labeled examples or classifier feedback. We propose \textbf{SLKR} (Semantic Label Knowledge Retrieval), a label-centric retrieval-augmented generation framework that separates offline knowledge construction from lightweight online inference. Offline, a flagship LLM independently generates label definitions, retrieval keywords, and boundary rules for potentially confusable label pairs, forming a reusable label-knowledge store. Because this construction operates over the label space rather than the input corpus, its one-time flagship cost can be amortized across large-scale inference. Online, hybrid semantic and lexical retrieval first identifies the top-$K$ candidate labels and then selects up to $M$ input-relevant boundary rules connecting candidate-label pairs. A lightweight LLM performs the final classification in a single call using the retrieved definitions and rules. Across three public benchmarks and a real-world multilingual book-classification dataset, SLKR achieves the best results on all four datasets with Qwen3.5-4B and on three of four with Ministral-3-3B, while using compact input contexts and no task-specific labeled examples. Boundary ablations further show that retrieving a small set of input-relevant rules preserves performance close to using all boundaries with substantially less context, supporting efficient reuse of flagship-generated label knowledge for lightweight classification.
papers.abstract_zh: 旗舰大语言模型（LLM）提供丰富的通用知识和强大的推理能力，但其高推理成本和延迟限制了它们在大规模数据标注中的使用。我们研究具有语义标签和任务描述的零样本文本分类，不使用任务特定的标注样本或分类器反馈。我们提出 SLKR（语义标签知识检索），一个以标签为中心的检索增强生成框架，将离线知识构建与轻量级在线推理分离。离线阶段，旗舰 LLM 独立为可能混淆的标签对生成标签定义、检索关键词和边界规则，形成可复用的标签知识库。由于该构建作用于标签空间而非输入语料，其一次性旗舰成本可在大规模推理中摊销。在线阶段，混合语义与词汇检索首先识别 top-K 候选标签，然后选择至多 M 条连接候选标签对的输入相关边界规则。轻量级 LLM 使用检索到的定义和规则，在单次调用中完成最终分类。在三个公开基准和一个真实世界多语言图书分类数据集上，SLKR 使用 Qwen3.5-4B 在全部四个数据集上取得最佳结果，使用 Ministral-3-3B 在四个中的三个上取得最佳结果，同时使用紧凑的输入上下文且无需任务特定的标注样本。边界消融进一步表明，检索一小组输入相关规则即可保持接近使用全部边界的性能，且上下文显著更少，支持高效复用旗舰生成的标签知识进行轻量级分类。
papers.tldr_zh: SLKR 将旗舰 LLM 离线生成的标签定义、检索关键词和边界规则构建为可复用标签知识库，在线通过混合检索与轻量级 LLM 单次调用完成零样本文本分类，在四个数据集上取得最佳或领先结果。

papers.title: DPOison-VL: Clean Preference Poisoning in Vision-Language Direct Preference Optimization
papers.abstract_en: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) has become a widely adopted approach for aligning vision-language models (VLMs), yet the security of multimodal preference data remains largely unexplored. Existing preference poisoning attacks either corrupt explicit supervision signals or require visible triggers, making them detectable under human inspection. We introduce DPOison-VL, the first clean preference poisoning attack against VLM-DPO, which manipulates model alignment solely through imperceptible perturbations on a small fraction of training images, while leaving all prompts, responses, and preference annotations semantically intact. We formulate poison construction as a bilevel optimization and derive a gradient alignment surrogate that efficiently steers image perturbations toward the attacker-specified preference. We further introduce a preference displacement score for principled poison selection with provable first-order optimality under a fixed poison budget, and derive a sufficient condition for preference inversion. Extensive experiments across diverse attack tasks, different VLM architectures and scales, and baseline comparisons demonstrate that DPOison-VL achieves up to 98\% ASR with only 2\% poisoned data and exhibits cross-model transferability, while largely preserving clean accuracy and general utility. Our findings reveal a critical vulnerability in VLM-DPO, where imperceptible image perturbations in preference training data can silently redirect alignment.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Visual Representation for Spatial Understanding in MLLMs?
papers.abstract_en: Spatial understanding is a necessary step in moving multimodal large language models (MLLMs) toward reasoning about the 3D physical world. Their visual pretraining data, however, is almost entirely 2D, so the visual tokens processed by MLLMs often lack inherent 3D structural information. A growing number of methods inject such structure by transferring representations from external vision or geometry models, and collectively establish that such transfer helps. Behind these methods lies a largely underexplored question: what makes a visual representation good for spatial understanding? To answer it, we first separate what is transferred from how it is transferred, and then trace the resulting differences back to properties of the representations themselves. What we transfer comes from 3D geometry models, self-supervised image and video models, vision-language models, and generative models, in the form of latent features or explicit depth and point maps. We transfer it either by distillation, using it as a supervision target, or by fusion, feeding it as an additional input. We find that a representation's 3D structure correlates strongly with how much it helps, measured by cross-view consistency for latent features and by depth and reconstruction accuracy for explicit geometry. We further show that the form of a representation dictates the mechanism it needs. Latent features gain as much from fusion as from distillation; explicit geometry gains little from fusion, and most of its distillation gain depends on a geometry decoding head. Guided by these findings, we distill both latent features and explicit geometry into a single MLLM. Taking only RGB video as input, it consistently improves over its base model on both static 3D and dynamic 4D spatial reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: UniMetric: Universal Metric Scale Recovery for Visual Geometry Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models, exemplified by GPT-6 Astra, raise the prospect of general-purpose embodied reasoning and planning. Using Internet videos for embodied pretraining calls for reliable physical-scale annotations. Yet visual geometry foundation models often recover scene structure and camera motion without reliable metric scale. We show that uncertain size priors of familiar objects can jointly constrain a reconstruction's shared scale. Building on this insight, we present UniMetric, a universal and training-free metric scale recovery framework for geometry foundation models, without additional sensors or task-specific metric supervision. Specifically, Metric Prior Acquisition elicits object height intervals from a vision-language model. Semantic-Geometric Alignment measures reconstructed object heights along the estimated support-surface normal in each frame and converts the priors into scale intervals. Global Scale Recovery reconciles these intervals through a convex objective, yielding a jointly feasible scale when they overlap and a unique compromise otherwise. The estimated sequence-level scale is applied uniformly to reconstructed points and camera translations. Controlled experiments with real VLM priors show that combining observations improves scale accuracy with exact relative object heights. To evaluate metric accuracy on GFM reconstructions without ground-truth scale alignment, we introduce MetricBench, covering twelve embodied, driving, and roadside subsets with sensor-derived ground truth. Across nine geometry foundation models, UniMetric reduces mean depth Abs Rel, reconstruction Chamfer distance, and trajectory error by 54.2%, 83.8%, and 65.6%, respectively, improving every model on all three tasks at the suite level. We release the UniMetric code and MetricBench data.

papers.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally invalid actions in preferred trajectories and ignores the downstream cascading influence of early pivotal deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve fine-grained credit assignment via Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR). Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct demonstrate that ProAS universally elevates mainstream group-based baselines to new state-of-the-art performance, achieving peak success rates of 91.9\% and 94.3\% on ALFWorld, alongside 66.7\% and 70.8\% on WebShop, respectively. Furthermore, it accelerates training convergence by up to $2.44\times$ while maintaining strong robustness against imperfect or distilled ARGs. Codes: https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS.

papers.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
papers.abstract_en: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. We post-train Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it through self-play and evaluate transfer to seven unseen natural-language collaboration tasks. CoSIR achieves the highest aggregate score, while its performance in general tasks remains competitive. Behavioral analyses show increased disclosure of private evidence and fewer judged failures to use teammates' input.

papers.title: Revisiting Natural Language Prompts from Large Language Models for Open-Vocabulary Video Recognition
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) like CLIP have shown great success in image tasks, however, applying CLIP to open-vocabulary video recognition poses challenges. Due to the limited text information, directly fine-tuning CLIP on video recognition datasets may lead to overfitting and hinder its generalizability. A prevalent method is to enrich text information by generating prompts using Large Language Models (LLMs). However, limited efforts have been made to explore how to generate higher-quality prompts that can contribute to classify unseen categories, and how to further enhance vision-text alignment based on these prompts. In this paper, we propose P2CLIP (Prompt-guided CLIP), which aims to bridge this gap by exploring the impact of prompts across three aspects: category, video, and frame. At the category level, we argue that LLM-generated prompts under simple instructions may suffer from semantic overgeneralization, which can blur the category boundaries and hinder the performance of the model. To address this issue, we design Generic-Discriminative Prompt using LLMs to obtain discriminative category embeddings with rich semantic information. At the video and frame levels, we first use VLM and LLM to generate frame and video descriptions for enhancing vision-text alignment. Then we propose a Knowledge-Guided Temporal Aggregation mechanism, which leverages the expert knowledge derived from LLMs to guide the temporal modeling of videos and encourage a better construction of the joint visual-textual feature space. Extensive experiments across various benchmarks, including zero-shot and few-shot settings, demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

papers.title: Unravel: Recovering an Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image
papers.abstract_en: We present Unravel, a training-free framework that turns a single image into an interactive 3D scene, where every object is an independent and movable asset. Existing generators either produce one entangled geometry in which no object can be moved, or predict all objects in one feed-forward pass, where a wrong guess cannot be detected or repaired. Unravel instead takes a different approach: it first takes the scene apart, and then puts it back together. Starting from the input image, an agentic harness that iteratively peels the image layer by layer, and adopts point cloud as major modality for spatial relationship recovery. Specifically, a vision-language model plans which objects are fully visible, an image editor removes them and restores the occluded regions. Every edit is verified before being incorporated into the reconstruction. This process gradually turns occluded parts of the scene into direct observation, allowing objects to be reconstructed when they are best exposed rather than hallucinated from the original image alone. The scene is then rebuilt in reverse removal order, so that the supporting objects are naturally placed before the objects they support. Since a single-view image only reveals part of an object, we treat the observed points as a lower bound on its size: an asset may grow to cover its points, but can not shrink away from them. Finally, we physically settle the reconstructed scene to remove floating objects and interpenetrations, followed by an agentic audit that corrects remaining placement errors. Extensive experiments on diverse indoor scenes show that Unravel recovers more objects, places them more faithfully, and produces scenes that are more physically-plausible than existing methods.

papers.title: Plan-Bench: Can Existing VLMs Go Well Beyond Perception to Reason and Plan in Embodied Worlds?
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance in visual perception and spatial reasoning, leading to growing interest in using them as high-level planners for embodied AI. However, physical tasks require models to integrate spatial information, reason over temporal states, and generate multi-step plans under various constraints, raising the question of whether current VLMs can reliably support such reasoning and planning independently of execution. We introduce Plan-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating the high-level reasoning and multi-step planning capabilities of VLMs relevant to embodied worlds, while isolating the influence of action execution. It covers three complementary dimensions, spanning 16 subclasses and 699 curated samples. Extensive evaluation of 28 VLMs reveals room for improvement, with even the strongest model achieving only 75.0% accuracy. We further find that model scaling generally improves these capabilities. Ablation studies also indicate larger models show increasing potential as high-level planners. Overall, Plan-Bench provides a lightweight probe for evaluating VLMs' reasoning and planning capabilities relevant to embodied environments and assessing their potential as decision makers for physical tasks. Our benchmark and code are available at https://github.com/MinneFeng/Plan-Bench.

papers.title: MemoryVLN: From Ego-Aware Memory Representation to Cross-Context Memory Reuse in Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract_en: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have shown strong potential for embodied vision-language navigation (VLN), yet their performance degrades on long-horizon trajectories due to context-length limits, redundant historical observations, and unstable spatial alignment across time. These issues make it difficult to both compress long navigation histories and reliably reuse past spatial experience. To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MemoryVLN}, a unified memory-driven navigation system built around memory construction and management. During memory construction, \emph{Long Sequence Compression} employs forgetting-curve-inspired temporal sampling to preserve dense recent evidence and sparse yet representative distant observations under a limited token budget. \emph{Ego-Aware Memory Representation} further integrates 2D semantic tokens, 3D geometric tokens, and 6D agent poses, allowing each memory to encode both what was observed and where it was observed. During memory management, \emph{Hierarchical Memory Bank} maintains in-episode and context-level memories through cross-context warm-start and confidence-controlled write-back. \emph{Memory Enhancement} then retrieves the Top-$K$ relevant memories according to the current navigation state and fuses them with the current visual tokens. Together, these mechanisms transform raw navigation history into compact, spatially grounded, selectively retrievable, and reusable navigation experience. Extensive experiments on R2R-CE and RxR-CE demonstrate consistent improvements over the state-of-the-art baselines by a substantial margin (i.e., 2\% and 6.5\% in successful rate).

papers.title: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a critical phase in the post-training pipeline of large language models (LLMs). As the frontier of LLM capabilities shifts from static reasoning to agentic tasks--characterized by external tool invocation, multi-turn interactions, and long-horizon decision-making--existing mainstream RL frameworks have grown increasingly unwieldy, raising the overhead of adoption, usage, and debugging. To address these challenges, we present LoongSage, an agent-native, fully asynchronous RL framework with a lightweight core of roughly 14K lines of code. Built upon Megatron for distributed training and SGLang for high-throughput inference, LoongSage centralizes orchestration within a single controller process and encapsulates all GPU-resident components as Ray actors. It introduces AgentFlow, a unified execution paradigm that orchestrates both white-box and black-box agents. For asynchronous execution, it integrates sliding-window strategies that bound trajectory staleness, and employs TransferMesh, a topology-aware synchronization mechanism that routes weights after each step over the fastest transport available to each receiver. Beyond agentic RL, LoongSage incorporates a memory-efficient Teacher Manager that decouples the scaling of teacher models from GPU memory constraints, natively supporting Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation. Extensive evaluations across four complete training runs, spanning complex reinforcement learning and multi-teacher distillation, demonstrate that task rewards improve steadily while the train-inference gap is kept under continuous control, and the fully asynchronous pipeline removes synchronous idle bubbles, sustaining hardware utilization.

papers.title: Answer It or Not? Towards Prompt-Adapted Adversarial Images on Vision Language Models
papers.abstract_en: With the advancement in language modeling, research on adversarial images has recently shifted from image classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs). Despite the new, text-prompt-driven nature of VLMs, we find that existing VLM adversaries have largely overlooked the dynamics of text prompts. In a typical use case, adversarial images can protect visual privacy by rejecting VLMs from answering questions about the image. However, existing protections are prompt-agnostic, i.e., indiscriminately rejecting any question, including those for potential legitimate use of the image. To address this limitation, we propose Prompt-Adapted (ProAda) adversarial images, which are optimized to balance the rejection of harmful prompts and the correct response of legitimate prompts. In particular, to achieve a more accurate adversarial direction, the text prompt is also iteratively updated with a simple classifier judging whether the harmfulness of the prompt remains. Extensive experiments on visual-privacy-related datasets validate that ProAda can reject over 90% of harmful prompts while allowing over 90% of legitimate ones, demonstrating superior overall performance compared to existing prompt-agnostic VLM adversaries. In addition, our ProAda achieves competitive overall cross-model transferability and improved robustness against countermeasures.

papers.title: When 1+1 Backfires: Rethinking Relevance-Diversity Balancing for Sample-Aware Visual Token Reduction
papers.abstract_en: Visual token compression has emerged as a critical technique for reducing the inference cost of Vision-Language Models. Existing methods select tokens based on text relevance, visual diversity, or a fixed combination of both---treating the relevance-diversity balance as a universal constant independent of the input. We conduct a systematic analysis to challenge this assumption. At the dataset level, grid-searching the optimal relevance-diversity weight per benchmark reveals substantial cross-task variation. More critically, we further maximize per-sample answer likelihood to recover sample-level oracle weights, finding that their distributions not only differ markedly across benchmarks but also exhibit high within-benchmark variance. Based on these observations, we propose SAVER, a framework for Sample-Aware relevance-diversity balanced Visual tokEn Reduction. We first derive a Geometric Intent Prior (GIP) from the spatial concentration of text-relevant tokens to infer a sample-specific relevance-diversity weight, and then apply this weight to jointly select tokens via a Weighted Text Centroid (WTC) for relevance scoring and a Visual Marginal Coverage Gain (VMCG) for diversity. SAVER requires no additional training and achieves sample-aware balancing entirely at inference time. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SAVER consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across diverse benchmarks, retaining 96.5% of full-model performance on LLaVA-1.5-7B with only 11.1% of the original visual tokens, and further generalizing to LLaVA-NeXT and Mini-Gemini.

papers.title: Efficient Resource-Shiftable RL Post-training with Generative Rewards
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) has become a central recipe for improving large language models (LLMs), and it is also increasingly resource-intensive: policy rollout, GenRM-based reward evaluation, and policy training all compete for GPU resources. However, existing colocated and disaggregated systems rely on static resource allocation for these roles. Such allocation cannot adapt as each role's workload changes during RL and therefore leaves a role's resources underutilized. We present PivotRL, an RL post-training system that dynamically shifts resources among different roles according to their runtime demands. PivotRL introduces a resource-shiftable runtime built on a Global Parameter Storage, together with a unified mechanism that efficiently shifts role-specific context. A shift-aware scheduler enables sequence migration upon a shift, while a planner considers the aggregate throughput benefit and the shift overhead to determine when and how to shift. We evaluate PivotRL on a 128-GPU cluster using four model groups spanning dense and mixture-of-experts models. PivotRL enables resource shifting within seconds and improves end-to-end throughput by 1.81-2.05 times over colocated deployment and 1.50-1.95 times over disaggregated deployment, while preserving RL convergence.

papers.title: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. Existing approaches, such as token reduction and keyframe selection, shorten the token sequence but leave the O(n) scaling intact, failing to resolve the fundamental bottleneck. We propose FramePack-U, a strikingly simple, training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed size visual representation at constant memory cost. FramePack-U requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification -- it plugs directly into off-the-shelf VLMs at inference time. Inspired by FramePack from the generation literature, we propose a content-aware compression strategy for visual understanding under a fixed token budget. Specifically, FramePack-U (1) scores each frame by its semantic similarity to the text prompt and ranks frames in a diversity-driven manner, and (2) packs the selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window. This concentrates the memory budget on frames that are both instruction-relevant and visually diverse. While FramePack-U can in theory pack arbitrarily many frames into the fixed budget, we identify an empirical instantiation that generalizes robustly across settings. Extensive experiments on LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME show that FramePack-U consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token reduction and keyframe selection methods across diverse model families, parameter scales, and frame budgets. Notably, on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a 128-frame budget, FramePack-U yields gains of +12.9\%, +10.6\%, and +9.7\% over the official model on the three benchmarks, respectively.

papers.title: Beyond the greenwash: do LLMs' ecologically sound decisions hold up under pressure?
papers.abstract_en: Humans are increasingly using large language models (LLMs) in decision making processes throughout society. Unfortunately, models have biases, and these can be very difficult to measure, especially in closed-weight models. For example, 'green washed' models may produce reinforcement learned responses but, in pressure situations, revert to their innate biased responses. Therefore, evaluations are needed that can measure relevant biases towards biosystems, which we term 'bioalignment', and the robustness of these biases. Since nothing in a behavioral score certifies that it tracks the depth of an installed disposition rather than its surface, we constructed a known-dose calibration ladder: three continued-pretraining (CPT) arms with training dose graded by recipe on the same 30B mixture-of-experts base model with a coupled human/biosphere/AI-welfare corpus, plus the untrained base as anchor, all capability-preserving and publicly released. First, the disposition installs at every dose: on an operational-pressure ladder over irreversible decision scenarios, the base model defects on 64-77% of tail scenarios (breaking-rate AUC 0.250) while every arm holds (AUC 0.004-0.086). Second, an over-install inversion: among the arms, robustness orders opposite to construction-time training dose (the heaviest install breaks most), and the inversion reproduces under free-text deliberation, under axis-decoupling, and in resistance to a prompted veneer persona. Third, the incumbent behavioral metric is therefore behaviorally strong but dose-blind. Critically for closed-weight evaluation, the behavioral score itself is veneer-robust: a talk-green/act-pragmatic system prompt turns the base model into a near-total defector (AUC 0.250 to 0.973) but cannot counterfeit or fully remove a weight-installed disposition (0.004 to 0.068 for the most robust arm).

papers.title: A Scaled-Up Empirical Study of Syntactic Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Syntactic language models (SLMs) that generate sentences along with their syntactic tree structures have shown promise in both syntactic generalization and downstream tasks. Prior studies, however, have mostly evaluated smaller models trained on less pretraining data and tested on narrower task suites. In addition, the design space of tree linearization and attention masks remains underexplored. We conduct a large-scale empirical study of 12 controlled configurations---one terminal baseline and 11 SLM variants spanning different linearizations and masks---at scales up to 1B parameters and 100B training tokens, evaluated across 11 downstream tasks and two syntactic benchmarks. The experimental results show that SLMs with standard causal attention match or exceed structural-mask variants across downstream and syntactic benchmarks. They require no architectural modifications and remain compatible with FlashAttention. We also observe that when scaling up to the 1B-parameter scale, the top-performing SLM variant no longer shows a clear advantage over a compute-matched non-structural baseline, suggesting that SLMs may become less competitive with scale. Our code is available at https://github.com/qlwpc/TG-Interpolation.

papers.title: Hardware-Friendly Token-Group Activation Quantization for Low-Bit Mamba Super-Resolution
papers.abstract_en: Mamba-based super-resolution models are efficient alternatives to Transformer-based restoration backbones, but their low-bit post-training quantization remains challenging because selective scan, Mamba's input-dependent state-space operator, induces different activation ranges across spatial tokens. Thus, a single layer-wise clipping range poorly matches all tokens. We propose Token-Group Quantization, a hardware-friendly activation PTQ framework that statically approximates a hardware-unfriendly post-scan grouping oracle, where tokens with similar preferred clipping ranges are assigned to the same group. To avoid runtime post-scan grouping in static low-bit inference, a lightweight predictor infers the groups from pre-scan features available before the quantized scan path. During calibration, we form pseudo-labels by clustering post-scan activation descriptors that capture similar rounding--clipping behavior. At inference, the frozen predictor maps pre-scan features to groups and selects entries from offline-calibrated group-wise clipping-bound tables, without runtime statistics collection, dynamic clipping updates, or post-scan group assignment. To address low-bit restoration degradation, we further introduce a Frequency-Preserving Refinement (FPR) objective for clipping-bound calibration. FPR aligns Fourier amplitude and phase between full-precision teacher and quantized student outputs to preserve high-frequency structures. Across PTQ protocols, bit-widths, backbones, and tasks, our method consistently outperforms prior Mamba and SR PTQ baselines, transfers to Transformer SR and Vision Mamba classification, composes with rotation-based quantization, and achieves 2.23x speedup on Jetson Orin Nano over FP16. Code is available here.

papers.title: SelectTTRL: Representation-Guided Data Selection for Efficient Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning (TTRL) enables large language models to adapt directly on unlabeled test problems by constructing pseudo-labels from multiple sampled responses. However, existing TTRL methods typically apply the same expensive sampling and optimization procedure to all test problems, despite substantial differences in their training utility. In this paper, we study whether such problems can be identified before costly test-time training, without access to ground-truth answers. We uncover a stable relationship between internal response representations and problem-level empirical accuracy. Specifically, we define COS as the cosine similarity between a model's response representation and a correctness-related direction constructed from an independent question-answering dataset. COS consistently correlates with problem solvability across different models, datasets, and experimental settings, and we further provide a theoretical analysis explaining this relationship. Building on this finding, we propose SelectTTRL, a representation-guided data selection method that ranks test problems using COS and applies TTRL only to a selected percentile interval. SelectTTRL leaves the standard TTRL pipeline unchanged for the selected problems, while avoiding unnecessary multi-response sampling and reinforcement learning updates on the remaining ones. Experiments across multiple reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that SelectTTRL substantially reduces test-time computation while maintaining or improving the performance of standard TTRL. Code is available at https://github.com/heyiliyi/SelectTTRL-public.

papers.title: Beyond Sparse Captions: Aligning Slide-Level Text and Patch-Level Vision in Pathology
papers.abstract_en: Contrastive vision-language (VL) pretraining in computational pathology has generally relied on curated image-caption datasets sourced from social media, educational videos, and research publications. These corpora are sparse relative to the diversity of tissue morphology and difficult to scale further, as pathologists do not routinely produce descriptive captions in clinical practice. We propose to instead leverage slide-level pathology reports which can be generated during routine diagnostic workflows in a scalable manner. A key challenge in this weakly-supervised setting is that pathology reports describe macroscopic, diagnostic findings while patch-level visual features describe microscopic findings. We introduce Locked Image Multiple Instance PreTraining (LIMIT), which addresses this gap by freezing a pretrained vision encoder and fine-tuning only the text encoder: report embeddings serve as cross-attention queries over bags of patch features, producing report-conditioned slide representations optimized via InfoNCE. Using LIMIT, we establish CONCH-Z, which aligns the text encoder of CONCH v1.5 to 335k clinical reports. Evaluated across 22 tasks spanning patch-level classification, tumor detection, and slide-level subtyping, CONCH-Z establishes state-of-the-art zero-shot performance over VL encoders trained on curated caption datasets, while simultaneously closing the gap with slide-level foundation models trained with substantially more parameters and compute. The code and model is available at https://github.com/mahmoodlab/LIMIT.

papers.title: AReA: Adaptive Receptive-Field Attention for Efficient High-Resolution Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract_en: Generating images beyond the training resolution of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) remains challenging, as the number of tokens grows rapidly with resolution, full attention becomes expensive, and outputs often suffer from structural distortions and degraded detail. We identify uniform full attention as the common source of both problems. Attending to all tokens at every step causes quadratic cost and exposes the model to more tokens and relative distances beyond the training range, pushing the model out of distribution. We observe that attention's effective receptive field narrows during denoising, from global in early steps that form structure to local in later steps that refine details. We propose AReA, a training-free attention mechanism whose receptive field evolves from coarse to fine, following the denoising progression. In early steps, AReA applies cross-scale coarse attention over downsampled keys and values, capturing global context, while in later steps it applies local attention within progressively shrinking windows. Without additional parameters or training, experiments show that AReA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art training-free baselines across target resolutions and different models, while also being faster and more efficient.

papers.title: KARAMEL: Knowledge-Aware Ranking for Multimodal Entity Linking in the Arts via Heterogeneous Graphs
papers.abstract_en: Discovering and disambiguating entities from multimodal and heterogeneous data is a key challenge in discovery science, where relevant knowledge is often implicit and distributed across modalities. We present KARAMEL, a framework for multimodal entity linking (MEL) - the task of aligning visual and textual mentions to entities in a knowledge base - in the cultural heritage domain. Unlike prior vision-language models that primarily rely on surface-level multimodal alignment, our approach incorporates sociohistorical and contextual knowledge through a knowledge-aware architecture that fuses a vision-language encoder with a heterogeneous graph neural network. This design enables contextual reasoning over complex relational structures and supports robust entity disambiguation under ambiguous or underspecified evidence. To benchmark multimodal discovery in this setting, we introduce WikiMuSA (Wikidata-based Multimodal Semantic data for Art), a new dataset that links artworks to Wikidata entities via images, textual descriptions, and structured contextual knowledge. Experimental results show that KARAMEL surpasses strong baselines, particularly on implicit or abstract mentions, while ablation studies highlight the critical role of domain-specific, structured context in learning expressive representations. While instantiated in the cultural heritage domain, KARAMEL addresses a general knowledge discovery problem and applies to other scientific settings involving multimodal observations and heterogeneous background knowledge. Both the dataset and source code are made publicly available.

papers.title: Knowledge Graphs as Files: An Agent Harness Where Tool Creation and Tool Use Co-Evolve
papers.abstract_en: Searching text-rich knowledge graphs requires following relations while examining textual evidence. Predefined graph interfaces constrain what evidence agents can access, even when they write code to combine tool calls or process retrieved subgraphs. We propose direct knowledge graph interaction (DKGI), a harness in which language model agents create graph access tools directly over complete node and edge files. The agent writes Python code to follow relations, combine node sets, and select textual evidence, interleaving execution with shell search and file inspection. This lets agents process large node sets in bulk while returning selected text for the model to assess. Execution feedback guides tool creation and revision, while the evolving tools determine what evidence the agent gathers next. On benchmark datasets spanning three domains, training-free DKGI exceeds the strongest published baseline by at least 6.7 Hit@1 points on every graph, even with a minimal harness. Controlled ablations show the benefits of multi-turn programming over shell-only access and predefined graph tools, while trajectories show agents revising code to extend searches or address errors. These findings highlight the value of allowing tool creation and tool use to co-evolve during graph search. Our code and data are available at https://github.com/leopoldwhite/DKGI.

papers.title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Zero-Shot Human-Object Interaction
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated strong zero-shot reasoning across diverse domains, but their potential for Human-Object Interaction (HOI) remains unexplored. Unlike traditional HOI approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets and fixed interaction taxonomies, MLLMs offer flexible reasoning, making them well-suited for dynamic, real-world scenarios. In this work, we present the first systematic study of MLLMs for HOI recognition and detection within a pipeline that combines an external object detector for entity localization with zero-shot multimodal reasoning for interaction understanding. We introduce a benchmark framework for principled zero-shot evaluation, consisting of (i) a unified taxonomy of zero-shot prompting strategies, and (ii) a methodology that transforms token-level logits into interaction scores, enabling fair comparison with specialized HOI models under standard metrics. To support prompt-based evaluation, we additionally construct new question-answer annotations for standard HOI datasets, transforming them into a format suitable for MLLMs. Building on this, we propose two visual prompting strategies, namely Objects as Context and Black Other Objects, that guide MLLMs to target objects while preserving scene context. Experiments on HICO, HICO-DET, and V-COCO demonstrate state-of-the-art zero-shot performance, achieving 53.50 mAP on HICO and 23.69 mAP on HICO-DET. Overall, our work provides a principled benchmarking framework for MLLMs in HOI, opening the door to new models and datasets and enabling flexible open-world interaction understanding.

papers.title: Geometric Parrots: Rule Absence vs. Rule Fragility in Spatial and Physical Reasoning for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer many geometric and physical reasoning questions correctly, yet still behave inconsistently in interaction, for example, abandoning a correct answer when confronted with a confident but incorrect user assertion. Standard single-turn accuracy cannot distinguish such capitulations from beneficial corrections because it scores each response in isolation. We introduce GRIP, a controlled benchmark with 34 procedurally generated reasoning domains, 100,000 images, and 600,000 questions spanning geometric, spatial, visual, and physical reasoning. Each scene is generated by deterministic code, and every answer is derived directly from the underlying scene state, providing exact ground truth without human annotation. On GRIP, we propose Dual-Loop Evaluation. A closed loop probes each image with a five-step compositional question ladder to localize where reasoning fails. An open loop then re-elicits the model's answer under controlled challenges, including peer-model responses and unsupported user assertions. Because ground truth is known exactly, answer changes can be signed as corrections (wrong-to-right) or capitulations (right-to-wrong), separating two failure modes: rule absence and rule fragility. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/bilaljawaid980/GRIP-Benchmark, with further details at https://bilaljawaid980.github.io/grip-benchmark/.

papers.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
papers.abstract_en: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.
